etymology: Named after Duane Gish, who debated by assertion density: more claims per minute than anyone could answer.
committed_when: A format with fixed time and a live audience.
tell: The reply is dozens of claims and no thread; the answer addresses four and looks evasive about the rest.
counter: Answer one claim at length and say the rest are unanswered rather than answered. Quantity was the tactic; refusing it is the counter.
senses: Overwhelming an opponent with a flood of dubious claims so that answering all of them is impossible in the time available.
It works on arithmetic, not argument. Each claim takes ten seconds to make and ten minutes to check, and the format does not care that they are not equally cheap.
example: *“Fourteen points: the vote, the machines, the ballots, the envelopes, the couriers…”* Fourteen claims, ninety seconds, one of them true.

confused_with.tell: Ad nauseam repeats one claim; the gallop produces a new one every sentence.
